key_insight: In laser-TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel, higher laser power and current increase molten-pool convection and penetration, while higher welding speed reduces heat input and shrinks the weld, with clear impacts on arc stability.
engineering_relevance: The study provides process-window guidance for controlling weld shape, molten-pool flow, and arc behavior in low-thermal-expansion Invar components used for aerospace composite molds.
method: Numerical simulation of molten-pool morphology and fluid flow
High-speed photography of arc and pool behavior during welding
Parameter sweep across laser power, welding speed, and current
evidence_signal: The abstract reports simulation and high-speed imaging evidence over laser power (5–6 kW), welding speed (0.5–0.8 m/min), and current (150–170 A), linking these settings to penetration, weld width, flow intensity, and arc deflection/stability.
watch_item: The conclusions are based on the tested parameter ranges, so transfer to other joint geometries, thicknesses, or material states may require re-optimization.
paper_title: Molten pool dynamic behavior and arc characteristics in laser-TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel
